newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money steady, gilt prices seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money steady, gilt prices seen rising.

text.p: Indian call money was quoted in the 4.5-4.75 percent range in early Tuesday trade and dealers said they expected call money to be steady during the day.
Dealers said call money had eased from last week's levels above 9.0 percent as a repurchase of securities by the central bank had injected liquidity into banks.
The Reserve Bank of India on Saturday reversed a repo transaction worth 51.5 billion rupees conducted last Monday.
Dealers said they expected prices of government securities to rise on Tuesday on demand driven by low call money rates.
"Given the current level of call money, there will definitely be some demand for securities today....prices will go up," said the chief dealer at a state-run bank.
